title: AI 要跨越盧比孔河了嗎？自我成長的 AI 離我們多遠 (下集)

caption_text_source.note: YouTube advertises a zh-TW track without the ASR flag on the original 2026 watch page. The archived metadata identifies the same video and source VTT by ID and language. The VTT manifest includes a few cues absent from the indexed CSV. Each cited start below is present in both the identified lecture and the indexed selection.

topic_alignment.paraphrase: Lee names SEAL. The same underlying language model can solve a task and propose a self-edit. At 2482.046 seconds he describes generating several proposals, applying each, scoring the resulting models and feeding those outcomes back as rewards. The 2430-second frame contains the SEAL outer-loop diagram. Its heading in the recording differs from the released slide.

Lee recaps the argument that both the agent and its improvement rule can change. He calls these two levels at 2535.499 seconds. At 2540 seconds the storyboard shows the agent trajectory along the top and the linked improvement modules below it.

Lee introduces biological evolution as an analogy. He compares the parameters that influence learning to genes and refers to lifetime changes in neural connections and selection across generations. At 2660 seconds the frame shows the two groups of people and the two DNA drawings. This topic comes after the equation discussed on PDF p.49.

Lee turns from the video pointers to a formal learning process. At 2585.549 seconds he denotes the parameters that govern learning by phi. At 2593.691–2609.640 he explains that the function maps old parameters to new ones. From 2626.390 seconds he discusses improving phi. At 2600 seconds the frame shows the neural-network rows and the first parameter-update expression.

Lee explicitly directs listeners to the two earlier 2021 lectures from 2565.729 to 2574.071 seconds. The storyboard already shows both linked thumbnails at 2560 seconds and still displays them at 2570 seconds. This pointer occurs before the general update equations and the biology analogy.
